title: Late-Payment Grace for Comfort Club Members on Repair and Emergency Service Calls
content:
**Collections bulletin.** On Repair and Emergency Service Calls invoices, the late-payment grace is the number of calendar days after a call's completion date that must be passed before a late-payment charge is owed. It depends on the customer's Comfort Club standing under Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements and on how the agreement's dues are drafted. The records read are the agreement's status and the dues payment entries on its dues ledger, with their payment method and posting date.

**Rule.** The late-payment grace is:

- 45 days for a customer with an active Comfort Club agreement whose dues were drafted by bank autopay three or more times in the last 3 months;
- 40 days for any other customer with an active agreement;
- the class's 30 days for every other customer.

A draft is within the last 3 months while fewer than 3 whole calendar months have passed from its posting date to the date of handling.

| Customer | Bank autopay dues drafts in the last 3 months | Late-payment grace |
|---|---|---|
| Active agreement | 3 or more | 45 days |
| Active agreement | 0, 1 or 2 | 40 days |
| No active agreement | — | 30 days |

## Boundaries

- Three autopay drafts in the window give 45 days. Two give 40 days.
- A draft posted 2 whole months and some days before the date of handling is within the window. One posted 3 whole months before is not.
- With a 45-day grace, nothing is owed on day 45 after completion, and the first charging period begins on day 46.

## Example (hypothetical)

A member on monthly autopay whose dues were drafted in each of the last three months has a 45-day grace. If the member switched to paying by card last month, only two autopay drafts fall in the window and the grace is 40 days.
